title: Searched "image pixlizer". Got a TED Talk on whether Red Bull contains bull sperm.
context: Someone googled an image pixelation tool. AI Overview answered a myth about energy drinks instead.

exchanges.response:
No, Red Bull does not contain bull sperm or any animal-derived ingredients.
The widespread rumor that Red Bull uses bull semen or fluid from bull testicles stems from a misunderstanding of one of its key ingredients: taurine.

Where the Myth Came From
The Name: The word "taurine" comes from taurus, the Latin word for bull or ox.

roast: The query was "image pixlizer." Google even offered "Including results for image pixelate." The organic links were PineTools and Resize Pixel. Then AI Overview opened with bull sperm.
Not a typo in the overview. Not a sideways citation. A full myth-bust complete with etymology, ox bile, and a "Where the Myth Came From" header. For a pixelate tool.

Somewhere between the search bar and the sparkle icon, Gemini decided the user needed reassurance about Red Bull's ingredient list. Nobody asked. Nobody was thinking about taurine. Pixelate was right there.
Full Fact and ThoughtCo got cited under a query that has nothing to do with energy drinks. The sources are real. The relevance is not.
verdict: Asked for a pixelator. Got a semen FAQ.
